note: City water-supply lake west of Hamilton with an MDC fishing dock and boat ramp. The primitive camping area on the west side is a walk-in campground maintained by the city; no road or parking lot reaches it on MDC's map. --Claude
summary: DROP CANDIDATE (walk-in, not drive-in): MDC brochure (11/2025) 'A walk-in campground (primitive) maintained by the city is available to campers on the western side of the lake'; map (04/12) shows the Primitive Camping Area as a hatched field between the lake and US 36 with no road or lot to it; the only lot (1888) is the boat-ramp lot across the lake. Waterfront if kept: the lakeview holds. Phone matches.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (walk-in): area page 'Things to Do When You Visit: Camping: Individual Campsites' (no 3CSR 10-11 rule 140 listed - a city-owned Community Assistance Program lake), but MDC's own brochure (dated 11/2025): 'A walk-in campground (primitive) maintained by the city is available to campers on the western side of the lake.' Map (04/12): the 'Primitive Camping Area' is a hatched field on the west shore bounded by US 36 to the south, with no road, lot or parking symbol reaching it; the only lot (GIS 26: 1888) is the boat-ramp/fishing-dock lot on NW Golf Course Dr across the lake, ~540 m away by air and further round. Imagery: a mowed field with tree lines; a pale gravel lane enters from the south past a group of houses and a fenced lot, which looks private/utility and is not on MDC's map. Not a drive-in campground on the agency's own description.

WATERFRONT (stored lakeview, if kept): GIS 582 / the pin sits in the mowed camping field ~70 m from the north shore and ~60 m from the east shore; the strips between are open grass with scattered trees, and the 85-acre lake is plainly in sight from most of the field - lakeview holds. Not on-water: no camping is marked within 50 m and the shoreline has a tree fringe.
